fields.description: Authentication configuration for the tool's outbound calls (e.g. connector credentials reference). A LIST carries more than one credential on one connector (#1095) — an API that wants an OAuth2 token and a subscription-key header at the same time needs both. A single object stays valid and behaves as a list of one, so every stored connector keeps working.
fields.name: authConfig

fields.description: Whether the tool is always in the agent's tool list ('always'), fetched on demand ('on_demand'), or left to its toolbox to decide ('inherit', the default).
fields.name: surfacing

fields.description: Id of the toolbox to create this tool in, or null to leave it ungrouped. References a toolbox (GET /api/v1/toolboxes). A tool belongs to at most one. Moving an EXISTING tool is a separate endpoint (PUT /tools/{id}/toolbox), where an explicit null means 'take it out of its box'.
fields.name: toolboxId

fields.description: Which of this tool's `implementation` settings may differ per environment (#1641 B15). Declaring one puts it on the deployment screen's Values tab, where each environment states its own; the value itself never travels in the tool. Omit to leave unchanged; send `[]` to declare none.

items.description: One setting that may differ per environment.

fields.description: Path to the setting inside the tool's `implementation`. `baseUrl` for a top-level field, `pagination.pageSize` to reach into a block, `queryParams.userID` or `headers.X-Tenant` to address one header or query parameter by ITS OWN key (never by position — the editor reorders them). On a toolbox the same path is applied to every tool in the box.
fields.name: name

fields.description: What this setting is called on the deployment screen, in the words of the person filling it in — 'Address of the service', not 'baseUrl'.
fields.name: label

fields.description: What an operator needs to know to answer it: what the value means, and where to find this environment's own.
fields.name: description

fields.description: How the deployment screen should edit it: text, long-text, email, url, number, yes-no, date, datetime, time, choice or multi-choice. Omit to let the screen read it off the value the branch already carries, which is right for almost every connector field — a `timeout: 30` is a number whether or not anybody says so. State it only where the value it will BECOME differs from the one it holds today.
fields.name: kind

fields.description: Ignored. A value is the branch's standard until an environment states its own, so there is nothing for it to be missing and nothing it can hold up. Set the standard you want, and override it where an environment differs.
fields.name: environmentRequired
environmentValues

rules.message: Cannot publish connector: Set the connector's side effects (read-only or performs actions) before publishing.

The tool's current code has not passed a clean dry-run yet. Dry-run it on a sample input and fix any error first. Only a dry-run of the tool's STORED code counts (POST /api/v1/tools/{id}/dry-run, or the Builder's dry_run_tool) — running caller-supplied code through /tools/execute deliberately does not, since that code need not be the tool's own.

Cannot publish evaluator: it does not declare a branch choice. An evaluator must declare an implementation: either a `run` function that returns a branch id, or a builtin reference to a house evaluator.
The tool has no implementation yet.

Cannot publish validator: it does not declare a strict pass/fail verdict. A validator must declare an implementation: either a `run` function that returns a pass/fail verdict, or a builtin reference to a house validator.

fields.description: Id of the toolbox to move this tool into, or null to ungroup it. Required — there is no 'leave unchanged' here, which is precisely why this is a separate endpoint from PUT /tools/{id}.
fields.name: toolboxId

fields.description: Version the edit is based on; a stale value is rejected with HTTP 409 (optimistic locking).
